title: Bear Gap off the Highs
teaches: The bear gap off the highs as we teach it today: a read, not a trade. The first gap down since a top that closes down 5% or more in the lower half leaves a zone of resistance. A close above the zone's top edge fills the gap and the read is off. The fall is measured, not traded; a retest short stays under the 200-day, needs the market's help, and is never taken at the gap-day close by reflex.

walkthroughs.title: VRSN, July 2008: the full window
steps: VRSN had a top on 2008-06-04. On 2008-07-07 it opened 3.4% lower and closed down 9.5% on 6.1x volume.
A full window: the day's high stayed under the prior low. The zone ran from 35.52 up to the prior close, 36.74.
On 2008-07-11 the bounce was rejected at the zone's bottom edge. That is the read.
A study short from there did well, but our ten examples are chosen winners. We teach the read, not the entry.

walkthroughs.title: DLTR, January 2020: the cleanest chart
steps: DLTR topped on 2019-10-22, then sat 5.1% off it. On 2019-11-26 it opened 14.8% lower and closed down 15.2% on 15.1x volume.
A full window with a zone from 98.98 to 112.39. The first gap since the top, and it is still open.
A flat five-week bounce rose to the 20-day, 94.25, under the 200-day. On 2020-01-02 it was rejected.
A study short did well, but the tail of the move was the 2020 market's. We teach the read, not the entry.

walkthroughs.title: CIEN, September 2017: a good gap in a strong market
steps: CIEN opened 8.7% lower on 2017-08-31 and closed down 11.0% on 11.0x volume. A textbook gap day.
Nineteen sessions later it was rejected at the 20-day EMA. The stock sat under its own 200-day, so the stock rule passed.
QQQ closed 1.0% above its 50-day. That is a strong market, so the short had no help from it.
A study short off that rejection was stopped the next session. A good gap is not enough.

questions.q: As we teach it today, what is a bear gap off the highs?
choices: A level to read, not a trade
A short to take at the close
A long to buy under the gap
A pattern we have dropped
questions.answer: A level to read, not a trade
questions.why: A level to read, not a trade. Today the app defines no trade, and the fall is measured, not traded.
questions.lesson_line: Today the bear gap is a level to read. The fall is measured, not traded.

wrong.A short to take at the close: Shorting the gap-day close by reflex is the mistake we warn against.
wrong.A long to buy under the gap: Buying right under an open bear gap is a long-side mistake.
wrong.A pattern we have dropped: We still teach it. It is a level, and it matters most for stocks you own or want to buy.

questions.q: Today our lesson gives you a short entry for the bear gap.
questions.why: False. Today there is no entry. The lesson shows the level, and the fall is measured, not traded.
questions.lesson_line: No entry today. Learn to read the level first.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A close above the top edge of the gap zone ___ the gap.
questions.why: Fills. A close above the zone's top edge fills the gap, and the level and any short are off.
questions.lesson_line: A close over the zone's top edge fills the gap. The read is off.

questions.q: Under an open gap down, what does the gap zone tend to act as?
choices: Resistance
Support
A price target
A trend line
questions.why: Resistance. The first rally into the zone is where trapped buyers sell. Outside sources describe the same weak spot.
questions.lesson_line: An open gap down leaves resistance overhead.

wrong.Support: Support is what a gap up leaves behind. A gap down leaves resistance.
wrong.A price target: A gap zone is a level where price struggles, not a place price aims for.
wrong.A trend line: A gap is a zone of prices, not a line drawn through highs or lows.

questions.q: A bear gap day should close in the lower half of its range.
questions.why: True. A gap day that closes weak shows the sellers won. Fleckenstein asked for the same close.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day closes in the lower half of its range.

questions.q: What makes a daily down gap a full window?
choices: Its high stays under yesterday's low
The open is under yesterday's close
The close is under yesterday's close
The open is under yesterday's high
questions.answer: Its high stays under yesterday's low
questions.why: The whole day's high stays under yesterday's low. That is the stricter form of a bear gap.
questions.lesson_line: A full window leaves no overlap with yesterday's range.

wrong.The open is under yesterday's close: That is only a partial gap down. A window needs the whole day under yesterday's low.
wrong.The close is under yesterday's close: A lower close alone is an ordinary down day.
wrong.The open is under yesterday's high: That can happen with no gap at all.

questions.q: Which gap do we read first off a top?
choices: The first gap down since the top
The third gap off the same top
Any gap down in a long decline
A gap down inside a base
questions.answer: The first gap down since the top
questions.why: The first gap down since the top. Later gaps off the same top did worse.
questions.lesson_line: Read the first crack off the top, not the third.

wrong.The third gap off the same top: Later gaps off the same top did worse.
wrong.Any gap down in a long decline: Off the highs means off a top, not a decline already well under way.
wrong.A gap down inside a base: A base has no top to gap away from. The read starts from a top.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The gap day closes down at least ___ and in the lower half of its range.
questions.why: 5%. The gap day closes down at least 5% and in the lower half of its range.
questions.lesson_line: Down at least 5%, in the lower half.

questions.q: A stock you own gaps down off its highs. What is that gap?
choices: A warning; the stop decides
A signal to buy more shares
A reason to widen your stop
Nothing; gaps do not matter
questions.why: A warning. For a holder, a bear gap off highs is a warning, so you manage it by your stop and trail.
questions.lesson_line: A bear gap on your stock is a warning. The stop does the rest.

wrong.A signal to buy more shares: We never add when down. It is one price with one stop.
wrong.A reason to widen your stop: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.Nothing; gaps do not matter: A gap off the highs is a real change. It leaves resistance overhead.

questions.q: For a long, buying right under an open bear gap is a good entry.
questions.why: False. Wait for the fill or a base under it. An open bear gap is resistance overhead.
questions.lesson_line: Do not buy right under an open bear gap. Wait for the fill or a base.

questions.q: A bear gap fills within days. What does a quick fill say?
choices: The buyers are strong
The sellers are strong
The gap was a partial gap
Gaps always fill quickly
questions.why: The buyers are strong. A quick fill is strength, and the level and any short are off.
questions.lesson_line: A quick fill is strength. The level is gone.

wrong.The sellers are strong: A quick fill means the sellers lost the gap.
wrong.The gap was a partial gap: Partial or full describes the size of the gap, not how fast it fills.
wrong.Gaps always fill quickly: Not so. In Bulkowski's sample only twenty-two percent closed the gap during the bounce.

questions.q: A gap that opens under yesterday's close, but not under yesterday's low, is a full window.
questions.why: False. That is a partial gap down. A full window needs the day's high under yesterday's low.
questions.lesson_line: Under yesterday's close is partial. Under yesterday's low, all day, is a window.

questions.q: After what does a bearish breakaway gap form?
choices: An advance, a top or a consolidation
A long, slow decline to a low point
A single quiet low-volume day
A stock split or reverse split
questions.answer: An advance, a top or a consolidation
questions.why: After an extended advance, an extended top or a consolidation. Kell also ties a gap down from highs to a top.
questions.lesson_line: Breakaway gaps down come off tops and consolidations.

wrong.A long, slow decline to a low point: A gap in a long decline is a continuation, not a break from a top.
wrong.A single quiet low-volume day: A quiet day does not build the extended top the gap breaks from.
wrong.A stock split or reverse split: A split changes the price, not the trend.

questions.q: Do small and large down gaps behave alike?
choices: No; small ones tend to recover
No; large ones tend to recover
Yes; both keep dropping
Yes; both recover
questions.answer: No; small ones tend to recover
questions.why: No. Stocks tend to recover after small down gaps and keep dropping after large ones. Fleckenstein wanted a severe decline.
questions.lesson_line: Size matters. Small gaps recover; large ones keep dropping.

wrong.No; large ones tend to recover: It is the reverse. Large down gaps tend to keep dropping.
wrong.Yes; both keep dropping: Small down gaps tend to recover.
wrong.Yes; both recover: Large down gaps tend to keep dropping.

questions.q: Prior close 50.00. The gap day closes at 47.00. The close is down what percent?
questions.why: 6.0%. (50.00 - 47.00) / 50.00 is 6.0%, past the 5% bar. The lower-half test is separate.
questions.lesson_line: Do the division. Down 6.0% clears the 5% bar.

questions.q: A full window: the gap day's high is 44.00 and yesterday's low is 46.00. How wide is the window?
questions.why: 2.00. Yesterday's low minus the gap day's high. That is the open space between the two prices.
questions.lesson_line: A window is the open space between the two prices.

questions.q: What is a rejection candle?
choices: Touches the level, closes low under it
It gaps through the level and holds
It closes above the level on volume
Any red candle that nears the level
questions.answer: Touches the level, closes low under it
questions.why: It touches the level and closes back under it, in the lower half of its range. The bounce was turned away.
questions.lesson_line: Touch the level, close back under it, low in the range.

wrong.It gaps through the level and holds: Holding through the level is the opposite of rejection.
wrong.It closes above the level on volume: A close above is a break, and above the zone it fills the gap.
wrong.Any red candle that nears the level: It must touch the level and close back under it in the lower half.

questions.q: A bear gap leaves a full window. How does our lesson draw the zone?
choices: One band: gap high to prior day's low
A single line at the gap day's high
A single line at the prior day's low
A single line at the 200-day
questions.answer: One band: gap high to prior day's low
questions.why: One band. By our current default, the zone runs from the gap day's high up to the prior day's low, drawn as one zone. A close above its top edge fills the gap.
questions.lesson_line: The gap zone is a band, not a line. A close over its top edge fills the gap.

wrong.A single line at the gap day's high: That is the bottom edge of the zone, not the whole zone.
wrong.A single line at the prior day's low: That is the top edge of a full window, not the whole zone.
wrong.A single line at the 200-day: The 200-day matters for any short, but it is not the gap zone.

questions.q: Short the close, or wait?
choices: Wait; do not short on reflex
Short; sellers won on volume
Short, at half the usual size
Short; a weak close is the cue
questions.story: A stock gaps down 15% off its highs on 10x volume and closes near its low. The chart looks broken.
questions.answer: Wait; do not short on reflex
questions.why: Wait. The stop over a gap-day high is wide, the stock is stretched, and big drops bounced 28% on average.
questions.lesson_line: Do not short the gap-day close by reflex. Big drops bounce.

wrong.Short; sellers won on volume: Heavy volume makes the drop real. Real drops still bounce.
wrong.Short, at half the usual size: Smaller size does not fix a wide stop or a stretched stock.
wrong.Short; a weak close is the cue: A weak close is part of the read. It is not an entry.

questions.q: What do we call this?
choices: A News Failure, not a bear gap
A bear gap off the highs
A Parabolic Short
A partial gap down
questions.story: A stock opens down 6% on bad news. By the close it is back above the prior close.
questions.answer: A News Failure, not a bear gap
questions.why: A News Failure. It opened down on bad news and closed above the prior close. The news failed.
questions.lesson_line: Check the close. Back above the prior close means the news failed.

wrong.A bear gap off the highs: A bear gap day closes down 5% or more. This one closed higher.
wrong.A Parabolic Short: That is a climax gap up after a burst. This stock gapped down on news.
wrong.A partial gap down: Partial or full names the size of the gap. The close back above the prior close names this one.

questions.q: Does the gap day qualify as a bear gap?
choices: No; the gap was bought back
Yes; it opened down more than 5%
Yes; any gap down qualifies
No; it must close down 10%
questions.story: A stock opens 6.0% lower after earnings, then buyers step in. It closes down 4.2%, at 70% of the day's range.
questions.answer: No; the gap was bought back
questions.why: No. It opened down 6.0% but closed down only 4.2%, at 70% of its range. That is a gap bought back, closer to a News Failure.
questions.lesson_line: The close is the test, not the open.

wrong.Yes; it opened down more than 5%: The open is not the test. The close is.
wrong.Yes; any gap down qualifies: The day must close weak, down 5% or more in the lower half.

questions.q: Where must a stock sit against its 200-day to be shorted?
choices: Under it
Above it
Right on it
It does not matter
questions.why: Under it. Our rule allows shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short.
questions.lesson_line: No shorts above the 200-day. Under it only.

wrong.Above it: Shorts above the 200-day are barred unless the setup is a parabolic short.
wrong.Right on it: The rule is below the line, not on it.
wrong.It does not matter: It is a hard rule: shorts only below the 200-day.

questions.q: A bear gap read applies to a $6 stock that trades $5 million a day.
questions.why: False. We read only stocks at $10 or more that trade $20 million a day. A $6 stock fails both tests.
questions.lesson_line: Price $10 or more and $20 million a day. Anything thinner is skipped.

questions.q: Fleckenstein says to short the gap-down close at once.
questions.why: False. He says to wait for the bounce to exhaust itself, then short as the decline resumes. Bulkowski also shorts the top of the bounce.
questions.lesson_line: The short comes after the bounce, not at the gap-day close.

questions.q: A breakaway gap down on good volume will be filled soon.
questions.why: False. ChartSchool warns against that trap: a breakaway gap on good volume often stays open.
questions.lesson_line: Do not expect a quick fill. Many gaps stay open for months.

questions.q: Which market reading helps a bear gap short?
choices: Red or Orange
Green only
Yellow only
Any reading works
questions.why: Red or Orange. The short needs the market's help. In a Red market we are mostly cash and shorts below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A short needs a weak market. Red or Orange.

wrong.Green only: Green is the long-side reading. A short in a strong market gets run over.
wrong.Yellow only: Yellow means smaller and fewer longs. It is not the short-side reading.
wrong.Any reading works: A short taken in a strong market gets run over.

questions.q: In Bulkowski's falling-window study, how often did a gap show overhead resistance?
choices: 25% of the time
5% of the time
75% of the time
Every time
questions.why: 25% of the time. About one gap in four showed overhead resistance, so a gap is a weak level, not a wall.
questions.lesson_line: A gap is resistance about a quarter of the time. Treat it as a level, not a wall.

wrong.Every time: No gap is a wall. His page says 25%.

questions.q: Three up days to a high, then a gap UP on day four that closes red. Which setup?
choices: Parabolic Short; the climax gaps up
Bear gap off the highs; it gapped
News Failure; bad news gapped
Parabolic Long; the burst is down
questions.answer: Parabolic Short; the climax gaps up
questions.why: Parabolic Short. Its climax day gaps up and closes red after a burst. A plain bear gap has no burst before it.
questions.lesson_line: A burst, then a climax gap up, is the Parabolic Short.

wrong.Bear gap off the highs; it gapped: A bear gap gaps down. It has no burst before it.
wrong.News Failure; bad news gapped: A News Failure opens down on bad news and closes above the prior close.
wrong.Parabolic Long; the burst is down: That is the burst down with a climax gap down.

questions.q: Our study short in DLTR was 93.01, the stop 94.71. How far above the entry is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 1.8%. (94.71 - 93.01) / 93.01. A clean rejection candle gives a stop well inside the usual 3% line.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance in percent: the gap between stop and entry, over the entry.

questions.q: Study short at 93.01, stop 94.71. Where is 3R, where a third is covered?
questions.why: 87.91. One R is the stop 94.71 minus the entry 93.01. Three of those under the entry is 87.91, where we cover a third.
questions.lesson_line: For a short, 3R sits under the entry. Mark it before the open.

questions.q: Our study ran 359 retest shorts and 311 were stopped out. What percent were stopped?
questions.why: 86.6%. 311 divided by 359. The level is a good read, but the short off it is a hard trade.
questions.lesson_line: Most study shorts were stopped. Respect the stop, not the story.

questions.q: In our study of 359 retest shorts, about what share reached 3R?
choices: About a quarter
About half
About three in four
Almost all
questions.why: About a quarter: 25.3% reached 3R and 14.2% reached 5R before the stop. It is a hard trade even when the read is right.
questions.lesson_line: Roughly one in four study shorts reached 3R.

questions.q: Which line is the zone, and for whom?
choices: Support, for a long
Resistance, for a short
Resistance, for a long
Neither; gaps do not matter
questions.story: A stock gaps up out of a base. Weeks later it falls back into the gap zone.
questions.why: Support, for a long. That is Gap Support, a gap up whose zone is tested later as support. The bear gap is the opposite line.
questions.lesson_line: Same mechanics, opposite line. A gap up leaves support.

wrong.Resistance, for a short: That is the bear gap, a gap down. This stock gapped up.
wrong.Resistance, for a long: A zone under price is support, not resistance.
wrong.Neither; gaps do not matter: Gap zones are real levels. Which side depends on which way it gapped.

questions.q: Is this a bear gap short?
choices: No; shorts live under the 200-day
Yes; 12% is a big enough gap
Yes; earnings gaps always follow through
No; shorts are never allowed
questions.story: A leader above its rising 200-day gaps down 12% on earnings and closes in the lower half. A friend says to short it.
questions.why: No. Shorts live under the 200-day. A leader above it that gaps down on earnings is closer to a reversal buy.
questions.lesson_line: Above a rising 200-day, a gap down in a leader is not a short.

wrong.Yes; 12% is a big enough gap: The size of the gap does not move the 200-day line.
wrong.Yes; earnings gaps always follow through: Nothing always follows through, and the 200-day rule still bars the short.
wrong.No; shorts are never allowed: Shorts are allowed under the 200-day, in a weak name, after the bounce fails.

questions.q: What happened to the read?
choices: The gap filled; the read is off
The gap held; the read is on
The read is stronger now
Only the open counts, not the close
questions.story: A stock gapped down off its highs three weeks ago. The zone runs 44.69 to 46.86. Today it closes at 47.30 on strong volume.
questions.answer: The gap filled; the read is off
questions.why: The gap filled. A close above the zone's top edge fills it, and the level and any short are off.
questions.lesson_line: A close over the zone's top edge ends the read.

wrong.The gap held; the read is on: 47.30 closed above the zone's top edge of 46.86. That is a fill.
wrong.The read is stronger now: A fill is strength for the buyers. The read is weaker.
wrong.Only the open counts, not the close: The test is a close above the top edge.

questions.q: Does the market help a short here?
choices: No; QQQ above its 50-day is no help
Yes; the stock is under its 200-day
Yes; QQQ is above its 50-day
No; a short never needs the market
questions.story: A stock under its own 200-day gapped down off its highs. The bounce was rejected at the 20-day. QQQ is 1.0% above its 50-day.
questions.answer: No; QQQ above its 50-day is no help
questions.why: No. The stock met its own 200-day rule, but QQQ sat 1.0% above its 50-day, which is not a weak market. A short needs a Red or Orange reading.
questions.lesson_line: A good stock chart is not enough. The market must help.

wrong.Yes; the stock is under its 200-day: That meets the stock's rule. The market's rule is separate.
wrong.Yes; QQQ is above its 50-day: A market above its 50-day is strength, the opposite of what a short needs.
wrong.No; a short never needs the market: It does. A short taken in a strong market gets run over.

questions.q: A new short here?
choices: Skip; wait for the bounce
Short now; momentum is down
Short at double size
Short now, but with a tight stop
questions.story: After a gap down the stock sits 20% under its 10-day average, with no bounce yet.
questions.why: Skip. We skip a short more than 10% under its 10-day average. 43% of gap-day closes were past that line.
questions.lesson_line: Too stretched means wait. The bounce comes first.

wrong.Short now; momentum is down: Stretched stocks snap back. That is the case for waiting for the bounce.
wrong.Short at double size: Size never goes up on a stretched entry.
wrong.Short now, but with a tight stop: A tight stop on a stretched stock is easy to hit in a snap-back. The rule says skip.

questions.q: A new short two sessions before an earnings report is fine.
questions.why: False. We take no new short within 3 sessions of a report. Check the date even when the next report looks far off.
questions.lesson_line: No new short within 3 sessions of a report.

questions.q: Skip a short that is hard to borrow or carries a high fee.
questions.why: True. Popular collapses are often expensive to borrow, so we skip them.
questions.lesson_line: Hard to borrow or a high fee means skip.

questions.q: Right after a big market flush is the best time to press shorts.
questions.why: False. Do not be eager to short right after an unwind. Pressing shorts right after one feels dangerous.
questions.lesson_line: Never eager to short right after a flush.

questions.q: Which bounce into the zone gives a better short read?
choices: Light volume, less than the gap day's
Heavy volume, closing near its high
Rising volume every day
Volume does not matter
questions.answer: Light volume, less than the gap day's
questions.why: Light volume. Bounce days that average less volume than the gap day show weak buying.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet bounce is weak. A loud one is buyers in control.

wrong.Heavy volume, closing near its high: That is buyers in control, a pass or a lower grade.
wrong.Rising volume every day: Rising volume on the bounce says buyers are building.
wrong.Volume does not matter: It does. Fleckenstein wanted the bounce on declining volume.

questions.q: What does this bounce tell you?
choices: Buyers are in control; stand down
Sellers are in control; press
Nothing; volume is noise
The gap has to be a partial gap
questions.story: The bounce into the zone runs on more volume than the gap day and closes near its high.
questions.answer: Buyers are in control; stand down
questions.why: Buyers are in control. A strong, high-volume bounce that closes near its high is a pass or a lower grade.
questions.lesson_line: Strong bounce, strong close: stand down.

wrong.Sellers are in control; press: A strong close near the high is buyers in control.
wrong.Nothing; volume is noise: Volume on the bounce is one of the main tells.
wrong.The gap has to be a partial gap: Partial or full is the gap's size. It does not explain the bounce.

questions.q: How do we treat the third gap?
choices: Lower odds; later gaps did worse
Best of the three; the trend is clear
Same as the first gap
Only the first gap has a zone
questions.story: A stock gapped down off a top in March and again in April. Now it gaps a third time and closes weak.
questions.answer: Lower odds; later gaps did worse
questions.why: Lower odds. The first gap since the top is the read. Later gaps off the same top did worse.
questions.lesson_line: The first gap is the read. Later ones are late.

wrong.Best of the three; the trend is clear: Shorting late in the down cycle is a named mistake.
wrong.Same as the first gap: Later gaps off the same top did worse.
wrong.Only the first gap has a zone: Every gap leaves a zone. The first is the cleanest read.

questions.q: Short or not?
choices: Not a short; it is above the 200-day
Short; the gap is the signal
Short; the bounce day rejected
Buy; gaps always fill
questions.story: A stock gapped down off a high. The bounce day closes 5.9% above its 200-day.
questions.answer: Not a short; it is above the 200-day
questions.why: Not a short. A gap in a stock still above its 200-day is a pullback in a leader. It closed 5.9% above the line.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day, a gap down is a pullback, not a short.

wrong.Short; the gap is the signal: The gap is a level, and the 200-day rule bars the short.
wrong.Short; the bounce day rejected: A rejection above the 200-day is still above the line.
wrong.Buy; gaps always fill: Gaps do not always fill. Only twenty-two percent closed the gap during the bounce in Bulkowski's sample.

questions.q: What is wrong with shorting this bounce?
choices: The fall is large and big drops bounce
The volume was too heavy to short
The gap was too small to matter
The 20-day sits above the gap zone
questions.story: A stock gapped down 35% on 27x volume. Twenty-four sessions later it bounces to the 20-day, already 40% off its high.
questions.answer: The fall is large and big drops bounce
questions.why: The fall is already large, and big drops bounce. BMRN was 40% off its high and the 20-day sat far under the zone.
questions.lesson_line: After a big fall the 20-day is far below the zone. Late means risk.

wrong.The volume was too heavy to short: Heavy volume is part of the read. It is not the flaw.
wrong.The 20-day sits above the gap zone: After a drop this large the 20-day sits far under the gap zone.

questions.q: Bulkowski: once the dead-cat bounce completes, what does price do?
choices: Falls again, averaging 30% lower
Rallies to a new high within weeks
Goes flat for a year or more
Fills the gap at once, on volume
questions.why: It resumes declining, averaging 30% from the bounce high to the post-bounce low in 49 days. The bounce comes first.
questions.lesson_line: In Bulkowski's sample the decline resumed after the bounce, 30% on average.

wrong.Rallies to a new high within weeks: He found the decline resumes after the bounce completes.
wrong.Goes flat for a year or more: The decline resumes, averaging 30% in 49 days.
wrong.Fills the gap at once, on volume: Only twenty-two percent closed the gap during the bounce.

questions.q: In Bulkowski's dead-cat sample, how many closed the gap during the bounce?
questions.why: 22%. By 3 months 38% had closed it, and by 6 months 58%. Most gaps stay open for a while.
questions.lesson_line: Most gaps stay open through the bounce.

wrong.58%: 58% is the share that closed it within 6 months, not during the bounce.
wrong.5%: He found 22% closed the gap during the bounce.
wrong.90%: He found 22% closed the gap during the bounce.

questions.q: Kell calls a gap down from highs, followed by a Wedge Drop, a sign of a top.
questions.why: True. He says a gap down from highs, followed by a Wedge Drop, marked the 2021 top for DECK.
questions.lesson_line: A gap down from highs is a top warning.

questions.q: Which of these is the cleaner gap-day read?
choices: First gap, down 7%, lower-third close
Third gap, down 5.2%, 40% of range
First gap, down 3%, closed at the high
Second gap, down 6%, upper-half close
questions.why: The first gap, down 7%, closed in the lower third. It is the first gap since the top and it closes weak.
questions.lesson_line: First gap, big drop, weak close.

wrong.Third gap, down 5.2%, 40% of range: A third gap off the same top did worse.
wrong.First gap, down 3%, closed at the high: The close must be down 5% or more in the lower half.
wrong.Second gap, down 6%, upper-half close: A second gap did worse, and the close must be in the lower half.

questions.q: Bear gap or Parabolic Long?
choices: Parabolic Long; a burst down
Bear gap; it gapped off a top
Gap Support; it gapped on volume
News Failure; volume was heavy
questions.story: Four straight lower closes, two gap downs and rising volume. The fifth day gaps down again on the heaviest volume.
questions.why: Parabolic Long. Its climax gap down comes after straight lower closes and two gap downs. A bear gap has no burst before it.
questions.lesson_line: Count the down days before the gap. A burst down is Parabolic Long.

wrong.Bear gap; it gapped off a top: A bear gap is the first gap since the top, with no burst before it.
wrong.Gap Support; it gapped on volume: Gap Support is a gap up. This stock is gapping down.
wrong.News Failure; volume was heavy: A News Failure closes above the prior close. Nothing here says that.

questions.q: By our current default, a bear gap is an open at least 1 ATR under the prior close, not filled that day. Read it or pass?
choices: Pass; an ordinary down day
Read it; any open under the close counts
Read it; it closed red
Pass; it must gap up
questions.story: A stock opens 2.1% under the prior close, 0.89 ATR, and never trades back up to that close. It closes red.
questions.why: Pass. By our current default, a bear gap needs an open of at least 1 ATR. This open was 2.1%, or 0.89 ATR: an ordinary down day with no gap zone to defend.
questions.lesson_line: Under 1 ATR is an ordinary down day. No real gap means no zone to defend.

wrong.Read it; any open under the close counts: By our current default, an open under 1 ATR leaves no zone worth watching.
wrong.Read it; it closed red: A red close alone is not a gap day. The open must be at least 1 ATR under the prior close.
wrong.Pass; it must gap up: A bear gap is a gap down. The problem is the size.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Log it; the stop did its job
Widen the stop and short again
Short again at double size
Quit shorting for good
questions.story: A study short was taken on a clean rejection. A strong market stopped it the next day for a loss of 1R. The gap was textbook.
questions.answer: Log it; the stop did its job
questions.why: Log it. The stop is the exit and it only moves up. A textbook gap in a strong market is a planned loss of 1R.
questions.lesson_line: A planned loss is the cost of the trade. Take it and move on.

wrong.Widen the stop and short again: The stop is the exit. It never moves wider.
wrong.Short again at double size: Never add or double up. A new try needs a new setup, as a new trade.
wrong.Quit shorting for good: One planned loss is not a reason to quit. The market was the problem.

questions.q: Four study shorts lost, though each gap was textbook. What decided them?
choices: Bounce, market, distance from top
The size of the gap, nothing more
The date of the next report
Bad luck with the fills and slips
questions.why: The bounce, market and distance from top. In all four the gap itself was textbook.
questions.lesson_line: The gap is the level. The surroundings decide the trade.

wrong.The size of the gap, nothing more: In all four the gap was textbook. Size was not the problem.
wrong.The date of the next report: Earnings timing is a separate rule. It did not decide these four.
wrong.Bad luck with the fills and slips: Fills were not the issue. What surrounded the gap was.

questions.q: What is the read, and what is left open?
choices: A clean level; the fall is not traded
A confirmed short; enter now
A buy; the gap will fill
Pass; the volume was too heavy
questions.story: A stock gaps down 15.2% on 15.1x volume, the first gap since its top. The zone is unfilled. A quiet five-week bounce reaches the 20-day, under the 200-day.
questions.answer: A clean level; the fall is not traded
questions.why: A clean level. Today the fall is measured, not traded, so we read the zone, the bounce and the market before any short.
questions.lesson_line: Read the level first. The short is a later decision.

wrong.A confirmed short; enter now: Today the app defines no trade. This is a read, not an entry.
wrong.A buy; the gap will fill: Only twenty-two percent closed the gap during the bounce in Bulkowski's sample.
wrong.Pass; the volume was too heavy: Heavy volume on the gap day is part of the read, not a flaw.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: A warning; let the stop decide
Short more against your long
Add to the long near the low
Ignore it; it is above the 200-day
questions.story: You own a leader above its rising 200-day. It gaps down 9% off its high on earnings and closes in the lower half.
questions.answer: A warning; let the stop decide
questions.why: Treat it as a warning. For a holder, a bear gap off highs is a warning. Manage it by your stop and trail, and do not short a leader above the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A gap down on your leader is a warning. The stop decides.

wrong.Short more against your long: Shorts live under the 200-day. This leader is above it.
wrong.Ignore it; it is above the 200-day: Being above the line does not cancel the warning. Keep your stop.

questions.q: A Red market alone makes the gap-day-close short a good trade.
questions.why: False. A Red market is not by itself an edge. The gap-day close short did worse with SPY under its 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A weak market helps a good read. It does not rescue a reflex short.

questions.q: What is the read?
choices: A first gap and a zone to watch
A confirmed short at the open
A buy; the window will fill
Pass; the gap was too small
questions.story: VRSN had a top on 2008-06-04. On 2008-07-07 it opened 3.4% lower, closed 9.5% down on 6.1x volume and left a full window. It was the first gap since the top. Four sessions later it was rejected at the zone's bottom edge.
questions.answer: A first gap and a zone to watch
questions.why: A first gap and a zone to watch. A full window with a weak close, then a rejection at the zone, is the textbook read.
questions.lesson_line: Full window, weak close, rejection at the zone: the textbook read.

wrong.A confirmed short at the open: Today there is no entry. The lesson is the read.
wrong.A buy; the window will fill: The bounce was rejected at the zone's bottom edge, so it did not fill.
wrong.Pass; the gap was too small: A 9.5% down day on 6.1x volume is not small.

questions.q: The VRSN study short had a stop 3.2% away. What does our stop rule say?
choices: Skip, or size down a grade
Take full size
Move the stop to the day's high
Add a second entry
questions.answer: Skip, or size down a grade
questions.why: Skip, or size down a grade. A stop more than 3% over the entry fails the usual line, and VRSN was 3.2% away.
questions.lesson_line: A stop past 3% costs grade or size.

wrong.Take full size: A stop past 3% does not earn full size.
wrong.Move the stop to the day's high: That makes it wider still. The stop only moves up.
wrong.Add a second entry: It is one price with one stop. No adding.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. Read the last bar against the gap zone and the 20-day. Read it or pass?
choices: Read it; the bounce was turned away
Pass; the gap already filled
Pass; the gap day closed high
questions.answer: Read it; the bounce was turned away
questions.why: Read it. A 15.2% down day on 15.1x volume, the zone unfilled, a flat five-week bounce rejected at the 20-day under the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: A big gap, an open zone and a weak bounce: a clean read.

wrong.Pass; the gap already filled: Price is still under the zone. The gap is open.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. The last bar touched the declining 20-day. Look at where it closed in its range. Read it or pass?
choices: Pass; buyers are in control
Read it; it touched the 20-day
Read it; the gap is open
questions.why: Pass. The bounce day closed at 82% of its range. That is a strong bounce into the 20-day with buyers in control.
questions.lesson_line: A rejection candle closes low in its range. This one did not.

wrong.Read it; it touched the 20-day: Touching the level is half of it. A rejection candle also closes low in its range.
wrong.Read it; the gap is open: An open gap is not enough. The bounce day must be rejected.

questions.q: All ten of our scanned example gaps were full windows.
questions.why: True. All 10 scan examples were full windows, the stricter form: the gap day's high stayed under the prior day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Our clean examples were full windows, not partial gaps.

questions.q: Fleckenstein, Bulkowski and our lesson all agree on what?
choices: Wait for the bounce before any short
Short the gap-day close
Buy the gap-day low
Hold until the gap fills
questions.answer: Wait for the bounce before any short
questions.why: Wait for the bounce. Fleckenstein waits for it to exhaust itself, Bulkowski shorts the top of it, and we never short the close by reflex.
questions.lesson_line: The bounce comes before any short.

wrong.Short the gap-day close: That is the reflex short we warn against.
wrong.Buy the gap-day low: None of the three says to buy the low of a gap day.
wrong.Hold until the gap fills: A fill ends the read. None of them waits for it.

questions.q: Shorting the gap-day close and shorting the failed bounce are the same trade.
questions.why: False. The gap-day close runs into a bounce that averaged 28% for big drops. The failed bounce is a later, different entry.
questions.lesson_line: Same gap, different trade. The close and the bounce are not the same.

questions.q: Which stock had the bear gap day?
choices: Stock A; Stock B is a News Failure
Stock B; it bounced the hardest
Both; both opened down 6%
Neither; the news was priced in
questions.story: Two stocks open down 6% on bad news. Stock A closes down 5.8%, in the lower third of its range. Stock B closes 0.5% above the prior close.
questions.answer: Stock A; Stock B is a News Failure
questions.why: Stock A. It closed down more than 5% in the lower third. Stock B closed above the prior close, so the news failed.
questions.lesson_line: Same open, different close. The close names the setup.

wrong.Stock B; it bounced the hardest: A close above the prior close means the news failed. That is a buy, not a bear gap.
wrong.Both; both opened down 6%: The open is not the test. The close is.
wrong.Neither; the news was priced in: Stock A closed down 5.8% in the lower third. The bad news worked.

questions.q: Is this a full window?
choices: No; it is a partial gap down
Yes; it closed down 9%
Yes; it opened lower
No; it is a gap up
questions.story: A stock opens under yesterday's close but above yesterday's low. It sells off and closes down 9%.
questions.answer: No; it is a partial gap down
questions.why: No. It opened under yesterday's close but not under yesterday's low. That is a partial gap down, not a full window.
questions.lesson_line: A window needs the whole day under yesterday's low.

wrong.Yes; it closed down 9%: The close size does not make a window. The day's high must stay under yesterday's low.
wrong.Yes; it opened lower: A lower open alone is a partial gap at most.
wrong.No; it is a gap up: It opened lower, so it is a gap down.

questions.q: Which rules say no?
choices: The 200-day and earnings rules
Only the 200-day rule says no
Only the earnings rule says no
Neither; the read is clean
questions.story: A stock gaps down 8% off its high and closes in the lower third. It is the first gap since the top and the bounce is rejected at the 20-day. The stock is 3% above its 200-day, and its report is in 2 sessions.
questions.why: Both. Shorts live under the 200-day, and we take no new short within 3 sessions of a report. A clean chart does not beat two rules.
questions.lesson_line: A clean chart still has to pass the rules.

wrong.Only the 200-day rule says no: The report in 2 sessions breaks the earnings rule too.
wrong.Only the earnings rule says no: The stock is above its 200-day, which breaks that rule too.
wrong.Neither; the read is clean: The read is clean. The rules still say no, twice.

questions.q: A short whose stop is more than 3% over the entry gets skipped, or sized at the next lower grade.
questions.why: True. If the stop is more than 3% over the entry, skip, or take it at the next lower grade's size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop more than 3% from entry: skip it or size down a grade.

questions.q: On a bear gap short, our hard rule covers a third of the position at 3R.
questions.why: True. Cover a third at 3R. That is the hard rule.
questions.lesson_line: A third comes off at 3R. Know the price before you short.

questions.q: On a short, the stop moves to breakeven somewhere between 2R and 5R.
questions.why: True. Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven lives between 2R and 5R, not before.
